extracted.intended_audience: newspaper reporters, journalism students, and editors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting illnesses, surgical operations, and deaths (including obituaries) in newspapers, emphasizing informational content, human-interest development, and dignified treatment. Covers what belongs in this class of stories and how to interpret a life in an obituary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of illness-and-death stories
rubrics_metrics.description: In this class of news stories are included those concerning the illness or death of persons known in the community or in the world at large, as well as those dealing with illness, surgical operations, and deaths that are sufficiently unusual to be matters of general interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what belongs under the category: notable individuals, unusual medical/surgical incidents, and deaths/illnesses with wider public interest. Use this to judge newsworthiness of such items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary character: informative with human-interest allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories of this kind are primarily informative in character, but the importance of the personal element permits effective human interest development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance factual, informative reporting (who, what, when, where, why) with human-interest details (personal anecdotes, emotions) that help readers connect, without allowing sentiment to overwhelm facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pathetic (touching) phases to add value
rubrics_metrics.description: Pathetic phases of illness or death sometimes give value to news that otherwise would be of slight interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and incorporate genuinely moving or poignant personal details to elevate marginally newsworthy items; ensure such details are relevant and not exploitative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The seriousness of the subject demands dignity of treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism, lurid description, gratuitous detail or disrespectful tone. Maintain respectful language, restraint in graphic detail, and sensitivity to family and community feelings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary purpose: fact plus significance
rubrics_metrics.description: In writing an obituary the purpose should be not only to give biographical facts but to bring out the significance of a personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Go beyond dates and offices held: interpret and explain why the person's life mattered, cite major achievements and influence, and constructively interpret the meaning of their life and work for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a well-written obituary
rubrics_metrics.description: A well written obituary is a constructive interpretation of the meaning of a person's life and work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft the obituary as a narrative that places biographical facts in context, emphasizing the subject's contributions, character, and legacy rather than mere chronology.
